title: Checksum verification — Corruption Detection Scanner
description:
The corruption detection scanner hunts for damaged files and invalid structures before they poison results: truncated writes, bit-rot, malformed records, broken container formats. It walks the archive verifying checksums, parsing structures, and cross-checking internal consistency, then triages findings into repairable, quarantinable, and needs-human-judgment. Silent corruption is the archive's worst failure mode; scanning makes it loud.

This record documents the checksum verification approach: Recompute stored hashes for every file and flag any mismatch as corruption.

Teaching ladder rank 1 (foundations): this record explains the core idea in plain terms — what inputs the tool takes, what outputs it produces, and when it is the right choice for an archive task.
